title: AEOeye vs Peec AI: Which Should You Pick?
metaTitle: AEOeye vs Peec AI: Which Should You Pick? (2026)
metaDescription: Peec AI tracks AI answers daily from $95 a month; AEOeye is a one-off audit, $29 for five engines. Who should pick which, with prices checked 3 Oct 2026.
shortAnswer: Pick Peec AI if you need to track the same buyer questions every day and show a trend to a client or boss; plans start at $95 a month. Pick AEOeye if you first need to know whether ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity name you at all: a free ChatGPT check, then a $29 one-time report. They do different jobs, and most teams need the snapshot before the subscription.
intro:
This comparison rests on Peec AI's public documentation (pricing pages, docs and terms) as of 3 October 2026; we have not used Peec AI hands-on. AEOeye is our product, so we say plainly where Peec AI is stronger. On anything that needs repetition, it is.

Older comparisons, including the earlier version of this page, are out of date in two ways. Peec's documentation now describes [ranked recommended actions](https://docs.peec.ai/actions), so "it only diagnoses" no longer holds, and the old $89 and $199 price points are gone from its [pricing page](https://peec.ai/pricing).

sections.heading: Which should you choose?
sections.body:
Choose by the job. A recurring report on how AI engines describe your brand points to Peec AI; a first answer to "do the engines name us?" points to AEOeye. Our view: do not pay for tracking before you know your starting point.

- **Choose Peec AI** if you will review results every week, need a trend line for a client or executive, manage several brands, or want source and competitor detail across 50 to 350 prompts.
- **Choose AEOeye** if you have never checked, want one clear snapshot, cannot justify a subscription, or want Claude, Perplexity and Gemini answers in the same report without picking models.
- **Use both, in order,** if you are unsure: run the [free audit](/) first, and start a Peec trial only if the result says AI visibility is worth monitoring.

Tracking a brand that AI never names gives you a daily chart of zeros. Find out where you stand, fix the obvious gaps, then pay for the trend line.

sections.heading: What is each tool built for?
sections.body:
Peec AI is a monitoring platform: you define prompts, it runs them every day and charts what changes. AEOeye is an audit: we write the buyer questions, run them once and hand you the answers. One produces a time series, the other a snapshot.

Peec's [documentation](https://docs.peec.ai/intro-to-peec-ai) says it runs your prompts daily and reports three metrics: visibility (how often you are mentioned), position and sentiment. It collects data by UI scraping, which means driving the public chat interfaces with browser automation instead of calling APIs. [Web scraping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_scraping) is automated extraction of data from websites, and

AEOeye's free audit asks ChatGPT three unbranded buyer questions live and shows the full answers, the competitors named instead of you, and starter fixes. The $29 report, paid once, adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity, grows to ten questions (the free three are kept) and adds a fix roadmap. We test each engine at the default tier a free user gets, the same idea as Peec's logged-out approach. There is no subscription.

sections.heading: How do pricing and engine coverage compare?
sections.body:
Peec AI's self-serve brand plans cost $95 to $495 a month; the AEOeye full report costs $29 once. The bigger gap is volume: Peec's Starter plan collects up to 4,500 AI answers a month, while an AEOeye report collects 50 once. Coverage differs too, as the table and notes show.

- **Plans.** Starter, Pro and Advanced cost $95, $245 and $495 a month on monthly billing, or $80, $205 and $420 billed annually, for 50, 150 and 350 prompts. Each lets you choose three models and tracks daily. Enterprise is custom.
- **Cost per answer.** Peec defines monthly AI answers as prompts times active models times frequency, so Starter is 50 x 3 x 30 = 4,500. That is about 2.1 cents an answer at $95. Our report is $29 for 50 answers, about 58 cents each. By our arithmetic Peec is roughly 27 times cheaper per answer; you pay AEOeye for needing no setup and no commitment.
- **Engines.** The pricing page lists ChatGPT, AI Mode, AI Overviews, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini and Naver AI as the models a plan can use. Perplexity appears as an add-on at $30, $70 or $140 a month per extra model on the page's annual labels, and Claude Sonnet 4 and Grok appear only in the Enterprise column. A [July 2026 Peec page](https://peec.ai/ai-instructions) written for AI assistants says Perplexity is included in every plan. Peec's own pages disagree, so confirm your three models in the trial.
- **Commitment.** Peec's [terms](https://peec.ai/legal/terms-of-use) end a monthly plan at the end of the payment cycle, but give no automatic refund when a fixed term is ended early.

sections.heading: Where is Peec AI stronger?
sections.body:
Peec AI is stronger at everything that needs repetition or scale: daily sampling, history, source analysis, team reporting and data access. If you need a trend, a snapshot cannot replace it, however good the snapshot is.

Sampling is the structural reason. [SparkToro](https://sparktoro.com/blog/new-research-ais-are-highly-inconsistent-when-recommending-brands-or-products-marketers-should-take-care-when-tracking-ai-visibility/), working with the tracking startup Gumshoe.ai, had 600 volunteers run 12 prompts through ChatGPT, Claude and Google's AI 2,961 times. It found under a 1 in 100 chance that ChatGPT or Google's AI gives the same brand list twice, and advised asking each prompt 60 to 100 times and averaging. Ten questions run once is a sample of one; Peec's daily runs are built to average that noise out.

- **Sources and gaps.** Its pricing page lists gap analysis: sources that appear often and name competitors but not you, by domain and URL.
- **Actions.** The [Actions docs](https://docs.peec.ai/actions) describe a ranked list split into site audit, owned and earned work, each with its evidence.
- **Bot traffic.** Crawl insights read server logs to show which AI bots hit which pages.
- **Data access.** Its pricing card lists Looker Studio under Advanced; Peec's [API docs](https://docs.peec.ai/api/introduction) say API access is limited to Enterprise customers.
- **Agencies.** The [agency pricing page](https://peec.ai/pricing-agencies) offers plans of $245, $495 and $795 a month and lists free pitch projects for auditing prospects.

sections.heading: Where is AEOeye stronger, and where is it not?
sections.body:
AEOeye is stronger when you have no setup time, no budget line and one question: does AI name us? There are no prompts to write, no models to pick and nothing to cancel. It is weaker once you ask what changed last month.

- **No setup.** We write the buyer questions from your brand and category. Peec's [quickstart](https://docs.peec.ai/quickstart-guide) asks you to add your first 10 prompts and choose competitors.
- **Five engines, one price.** The $29 report covers ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity with 10 questions, plus a five-layer SEO foundation audit and a fix roadmap by PDF.
- **Cheap to be wrong.** The free check costs nothing and the report is $29; Peec's cheapest plan is $95 for one month.

The limits are real. AEOeye has no history, no daily runs, no competitor dashboards and no team seats, and ten questions is a small sample. It does not guarantee recommendations or write content for you.

A neutral note: when we checked Peec's own site for [AEOeye's crawler access study](/blog/ai-crawler-user-agent-directory) on 3 October 2026, peec.ai's robots.txt blocked no AI crawler and named none, /llms.txt returned a 404, and the served homepage HTML had no JSON-LD (schema added by JavaScript would not show in our fetch). That is a fact box, not a verdict on the product.

![A glass bathroom scale with a blue tape measure laid across it](https://images.pexels.com/photos/53404/scale-diet-fat-health-53404.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: How do you decide?
sections.body:
Answer three questions in order: do you know whether AI names you, will you review the data every week, and who else needs to see it? The answers point to one tool or to a sequence.

1. **Never checked?** Run the free audit at [aeoeye.com](/). If the three answers name you, you have something to protect; if not, you have a fix list.
2. **Named, and need to keep it?** Start a Peec trial. Read our [Peec AI pricing guide](/blog/peec-ai-pricing) and [review](/blog/peec-ai-review) first; plan limits decide the real cost.
3. **Agency?** Peec's agency plans and pitch projects are built for client work. The $29 AEOeye report is a cheap one-off for a pitch, if you need no client workspaces.
4. **Need tracking under $95 a month?** Compare the [other Peec AI alternatives](/alternatives/peec) and our [guide to AI visibility tools](/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools).

Whichever you pick, treat one run as evidence, not proof: ask again next week before rebuilding a page around one answer.

keyTakeaways: Peec AI tracks the same prompts daily from $95 a month; AEOeye is a free ChatGPT check plus a $29 one-time five-engine report.
Per answer, Peec is far cheaper (about 2.1 cents against 58 cents by our arithmetic); AEOeye's advantage is no setup and no commitment.
Peec's documentation now describes ranked actions, so the old "it only diagnoses" criticism is out of date.
Peec's own pages disagree on which engines each plan includes; confirm your three models in the trial.
Check where you stand first, then pay for tracking only if the snapshot says AI visibility is worth watching.

faqs.q: Is AEOeye a replacement for Peec AI?
faqs.a: No. AEOeye is a one-time audit: a free ChatGPT check with three questions, then a $29 report covering ten questions on five engines. Peec AI runs your prompts daily and charts changes. If you need a trend line or weekly reporting, you need a tracker like Peec. If you need a first answer, the audit is enough.

faqs.q: How much does Peec AI cost compared with AEOeye?
faqs.a: On 3 October 2026 Peec AI listed Starter at $95 a month, Pro at $245 and Advanced at $495, or $80, $205 and $420 a month billed annually, with Enterprise custom. AEOeye is free for the ChatGPT-only audit and $29 once for the five-engine report. AEOeye has no subscription.

faqs.q: Does Peec AI cover Claude and Perplexity?
faqs.a: It depends on which Peec page you read. The pricing page lists Perplexity as a paid add-on and shows Claude Sonnet 4 only in the Enterprise column. A July 2026 Peec page for AI assistants says Perplexity is included and Claude is an upgrade. Confirm in the trial. AEOeye's $29 report includes both.

faqs.q: Does Peec AI only diagnose problems?
faqs.a: Not any more. Peec's documentation describes an Actions page: a ranked list of improvements grouped into site audit, owned and earned work, each with supporting evidence and a brief. We have not used it hands-on, so we cannot say how good the advice is, only that the feature exists.

faqs.q: Does Peec AI have a free plan or trial?
faqs.a: Peec's pricing pages list no free plan. The brand pricing page ends with a Start free trial button, and its terms say trial length and limits are set by Peec. We found no trial length stated on its own pages, so check the length before you sign up.
